verdict.rationale: Supabase ships an official MCP server whose tools let agents query/manage the database and even scopes access via RLS when Auth is added (supabase-docs-1, supabase-docs-45), and Supabase's own engineers describe adding a read-only-by-default mode for MCP tools as a specific mitigation (supabase-comm-2) — showing the read/destructive distinction is a real, if reactive, design goal. However, a concrete documented exploit (supabase-comm-1) shows an attacker used a prompt-injection attack via the MCP integration to make an agent read a sensitive table by leveraging service_role access that bypassed RLS, and Supabase's own engineer acknowledged prompt injection remains unsolved even with guardrails (supabase-comm-2), directly contradicting the 'safely delegate' promise for destructive/sensitive operations. Missing for 10: independent verification that scoped read-only/destructive tool separation is enforced by default and cannot be bypassed, and evidence the fix fully closed the RLS-bypass vector.
